translations.text: The Book of Numbers of Moses. The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of testimony, on the first day of the second month in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, saying:
“Take a census of the whole congregation of the children of [?], according to their family lines and their ancestral households, counting their names, each person individually.
Every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army of [?]: you and Aaron shall count them according to their military strength, and they shall be with you.
There is to be one man from each tribe, each one chosen from the heads of their ancestral households.
These are the names of the men who will stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the children of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Reuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
These are those appointed from the congregation, the leaders of the tribes according to their ancestral families, the commanders of thousands of [?].
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been called by name.

They gathered the whole congregation on the first day of the month in the second year, and registered them according to their descent and their ancestral families, counting their names, every male twenty years old and over, each person individually.
Just as the Lord had commanded Moses, they registered them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The children of Reuben, the firstborn of [?], were recorded according to their family lines, their clans, and their ancestral families, counting their names, each person individually: every male twenty years old and over, everyone who went out to serve in the army.
Their registered total was 46,400.

And the children of Simeon, according to their family lines, their clans, and their ancestral households, counting their names, each person individually: every male twenty years old and over, everyone who went out to serve in the army.
From the tribe of Simeon, their registered total was 59,300.

And the children of Judah, according to their family lines, their clans, and their ancestral households, counting their names, each person individually: every male twenty years old and over, everyone who went out to serve in the army.
From the tribe of Judah, their registered total was 74,600.

And the children of Issachar, according to their family lines, their clans, and their ancestral households, counting their names, each person individually: every male twenty years old and over, everyone who went out to serve in the army.
From the tribe of Issachar, their census totaled 54,400.

And the descendants of Zebulun, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Zebulun, their census totaled 57,400.

And the descendants of Joseph, the descendants of Ephraim, according to their families, their clans, and their ancestral households, counted by name, individually: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out with the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Ephraim totaled forty thousand four hundred.

And the descendants of Manasseh, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Manasseh, their census totaled 32,200.

And the descendants of Benjamin, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Benjamin, their census totaled 35,400.

And the descendants of Gad, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Gad, their census totaled 45,650.

And the descendants of Dan, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Dan, their census totaled 62,700.

And the descendants of Asher, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Asher, their census totaled 41,400.

And the descendants of Naphtali, by their ancestry, by their clans, by their ancestral households, by the count of their names, head by head: every male twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out with the army.
From the tribe of Naphtali, their census totaled 53,400.
This is the census taken by Moses and Aaron and the leaders of [?]. There were twelve of them, one man for each tribe, according to the tribes of their ancestral households.
And the complete census of the descendants of [?], together with their army, comprised those twenty years old and upward, everyone who went out to fight in [?].
They totaled 603,450.
But the descendants of Levi, from the tribe of their ancestral family, were not counted among the descendants of [?].
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
For look: you must not take a census of the tribe of Levi, and you must not include their number among the descendants of [?].

And you are to appoint the Levites over the tent of testimony, over all its equipment, and over everything belonging to it. They are to carry the tent and all its equipment. They are also to serve in it and stay around the tent.
And when the tent is to move, the Levites are to take it down; and when the tent is to remain, they are to set it up. But any outsider who approaches it must die.
And the descendants of [?] are to camp, each man in his own assigned place, and each man according to his division and his army.

But the Levites are to camp in front, around the tent of testimony, so that sin may not arise among the descendants of Israel. The Levites themselves are to keep watch over the tent of testimony, so that sin may not arise among the descendants of [?]. The Levites themselves are to keep watch over the tent of testimony.
And the descendants of [?] did everything that the Lord commanded through Moses and Aaron. That is what they did.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

Each man is assigned to his division, according to their standards and their ancestral households. Let the children of [?] camp facing the tent of testimony, all around it, and let the children of [?] pitch their tents.
Those who camp first, on the south side facing the sunrise, are the division of the camp of Judah, with their forces. The leader of the children of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His forces, those who were counted, number 74,600.
Those who will be beside him are the tribe of Issachar. The leader of the children of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His forces, those who were counted, number 54,400.
Those who will camp beside him are the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the children of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His military force, those who were counted, totaled fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All those who were counted from the camp of Judah number 146,400, with their forces. They are to set out first.
The division of the camp of the children of Reuben is to be on the west side, with their forces. The leader of the children of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His forces, those who were counted, number 46,400.
Those who will camp beside him are the tribe of Simeon. The leader of the children of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His forces, those who were counted, number 59,300.
Those who will be beside him are the tribe of Gad. The leader of the children of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His forces, those who were counted, number 45,650.
All those who were counted from the camp of Reuben number 151,450. They are to set out with their forces in second place.
The tent of testimony is to be carried, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. Just as they camp, so they are also to set out, each beside the other, according to their divisions.
And the division of Ephraim’s camp shall be on the west side, with their military force. The leader of the descendants of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His forces, those who were counted, number 40,400.
Those who will camp beside this one are the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the children of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His forces, those who were counted, number 32,200.
Those who will be beside this one are the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the children of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His forces, those who were counted, number 35,500.
All those who were counted from the camp of Ephraim number 108,100. They are to set out with their forces in third place.
The division of the camp of Dan is to be on the north side, with their forces. The leader of the children of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His military force, those who were counted, totaled sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
Those who come beside this one are the tribe of Asher. The leader of the children of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran.
His forces, those who were counted, number 41,400.
Those who are to camp beside him are the tribe of Naphtali, and the leader of the sons of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His army, those who were counted, numbers 53,400.
All those who were counted in the camp of Dan number 157,600. They are to set out last, according to their divisions.
This is the census of the sons of [?] according to their ancestral households. The total count of the camps with their armies is 603,450.
But the Levites were not counted among them, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

The sons of [?] carried out all the instructions that the Lord gave Moses. They camped in this way according to their divisions, and they traveled in this way, each beside the others, according to their clans and their ancestral households.
And these are the descendants of Aaron and Moses at the time when the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab, the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron the priest, who were anointed and ordained to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord when they brought unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with Aaron their father.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Take the tribe of Levi and have them stand before Aaron the priest, so that they may serve him.
They shall carry out his duties and the duties of the descendants of [?] before the tent of testimony, doing the work of the tent.
They are to take care of all the equipment of the tent of testimony and the duties of the sons of [?], carrying out all the work of the tent.
You are to give the Levites to Aaron and his sons, the priests, as a gift. These are given to me from among the sons of [?].

You are to appoint Aaron and his sons over the tent of testimony. They are to attend to their priestly duties and everything at the altar and inside the curtain. Any outsider who touches these things will die.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

For look, I myself have taken the Levites from among the descendants of [?] in place of every firstborn who opens the [?] among the descendants of Israel. They shall serve as a ransom for them, and the Levites shall belong to me.

For every firstborn belongs to me. On the day when I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, from humans to livestock. They shall belong to me. I am the Lord.”
The Lord spoke with Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
“Count the sons of Levi according to their ancestral households and their clans. You are to count every male among them from one month old and upward.”
Moses counted them, he and Aaron, at the Lord’s word, just as the Lord had commanded them.
These are the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershon according to their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath, according to their clans, are Abram, Issachar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari, according to their clans, are Mothai and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their ancestral households.
The clan of Gershon, the clan of Libni, and the clan of Shimei: these are the clans of Gershon.
Their census, counting every male among them from one month old and upward, was 7,500.
These clans of Gershon are to stay behind the tent, on the west side, and camp there.
The leader of the ancestral household of the clans of Gershon is Eliasaph son of Adael.
The service that the sons of Gershon are to perform, and their responsibility in the tent.
And the curtains of the courtyard, and the curtain that is above the tabernacle, and all the rest of the work.
And Kohath had the clan of Abram, the clan of Izhar, the clan of Hebron, and the clan of Uzziel. These are the clans of Kohath.
According to their count, every male from one month old and upward numbered eight thousand six hundred, keeping watch over the duties of the sanctuary.
And the clans of the sons of Kohath are to be behind the tabernacle, on the west side.
And the leader of the ancestral household of the clans of Kohath was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
And their responsibility was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altar, the sacred utensils used in worship, what is used to cover them, and all the equipment.
And the leader who is to be over the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, who was appointed to oversee the duties of the sanctuary.
And Merari had Mahli and the clan of Mushi. These are the clans of Merari.
Their census, according to their count of every male from one month old and upward, came to six thousand fifty.
And the leader of the ancestral household of Merari was Zuriel son of Amachiah. Their encampment is to be behind the tabernacle, on the north side.
And the responsibility of the sons of Merari was the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, its pillars, its bases, all the equipment, and all their work.
And the pillars surrounding the courtyard, their bases, the pegs, and their ropes.

And those who are to be in front of the tabernacle of testimony, on the east, are Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping watch over the duties of the sanctuary and the duties of the children of [?]. And the outsider who touches them will die.
The total census of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command, according to their clans—every male from one month old and upward—came to twenty-two thousand.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Count every firstborn male among the children of [?], from one month old and upward, and take their number by their names.

And take the Levites for me—I am the Lord—in place of every firstborn among the children of [?], and the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the children of [?].”
And Moses counted every firstborn among the children of [?], as the Lord had commanded him.
And all the firstborn males, counted by their names from one month old and upward, numbered twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three in their census.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the children of [?], and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. Let the Levites be mine. I am the Lord.
And for the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three firstborn among the children of [?] who exceed the number of the Levites,
take five shekels per person, according to the sacred weight, counting twenty obols to the shekel.
And give Aaron and his sons the redemption money for those who exceed their number.”
And Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the children of [?], he took the money, amounting to one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, according to the sacred shekel.
And Moses gave the redemption money for those who exceeded the number to Aaron and his sons, at the Lord’s word, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Count the descendants of Kohath from among the descendants of Levi, according to their clans and their ancestral households,
from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old, everyone who enters service to do any work in the tent of testimony.
And these are the duties of the descendants of Kohath in the tent of testimony: the most holy things.
Aaron and his sons must enter when the camp sets out on its journey. They must take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of testimony with it.
They must put a covering of blue leather over it, spread a cloth entirely of blue over that, and insert its carrying poles.

And over the table that is set out they must spread a cloth entirely of scarlet, along with the dishes, bowls, ladles, and vessels used for pouring out offerings. The bread that is always laid out must remain on it.
They shall spread a scarlet cloth over it and cover it with a covering of blue leather.
[?] of blue, and they must cover the lampstand for lighting, along with its lamps, its tongs, its snuff dishes, and all its oil containers used in its service.
They must wrap it and all its equipment in a covering of blue leather and place it on the carrying poles.
And over the gold altar they must spread a blue cloth, wrap it in a leather covering, and insert its carrying poles.
They must take all the equipment for service that they use in the holy place, put it on a blue cloth, and place it on the carrying poles.
And he must put the cover on the altar, and they must spread a cloth entirely of scarlet over it.

They must put on it all its equipment used in serving at it: the fire pans, the meat forks, the bowls, and the cover, together with all the altar’s equipment. They must spread a covering of blue leather over it and insert its carrying poles. They must also take a scarlet cloth, cover the washbasin and its stand, put them in a covering of blue leather, and place it on the carrying poles.

Aaron and his sons must finish covering the holy things and all the holy equipment. When the camp sets out on its journey, the descendants of Kohath must then enter to carry them. They must not touch the holy things, so that they do not die. These are the things the descendants of Kohath must carry in the tent of testimony.

Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, is the overseer of the oil or the fragrant incense, the preparation of the daily offering, the anointing oil, and the supervision of the whole tent and everything in it, in the holy place, in every matter.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Take the clan of the tribe of Kohath; do not destroy it from among the Levites.
Do this for them so that they live and do not die when they approach the most holy things: let Aaron and his sons enter before them and assign each one his task.
They must not suddenly enter to look at the holy things and die.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Count the descendants of Gershon according to their ancestral households and their clans.
From twenty years old upward, up to fifty years old, register them, everyone who enters service to do the work in the tent of testimony.
This is the service that the clan of Gershon must perform and what they must carry:
They must carry the curtains of the tent, the tent of testimony and its covering, the blue covering spread over its top, and the screen used to cover the entrance of the tent of testimony.
and the curtains of the courtyard that are above the tent of testimony, and all its remaining equipment, and the utensils used for service. They are to do all the work connected with these.

At the command of Aaron and his sons, all the service of the descendants of Gershon is to be carried out in this way, according to the duties assigned to them. You are to list by name the things they are to carry.
This is the service that the descendants of Gershon shall perform in the tent of testimony. The duties they shall carry out shall be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
You are to count the descendants of Merari by their clans and their ancestral households.
From twenty-five years old up to fifty years old, you are to register everyone who comes forward to perform the work of service for the tent of testimony.

These are the things entrusted to them that they must carry, according to all the work they are to do at the tent of testimony: the frames of the tent, its bars, its pillars and their bases, and the covering for the entrance of the tent,

and the pillars of the surrounding courtyard and their bases, and the pillars for the curtain at the courtyard gate and their bases, their pegs, their ropes, and all their equipment for all their service. You are to list them by name, together with all the equipment for service that they are assigned to carry.
This is the service of the clan of the descendants of Merari in all their work in the tent of testimony, according to what is assigned to them by Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Then Moses and Aaron and the leaders of [?] registered the descendants of Kohath by their clans and their ancestral households,
from twenty-five years old and upward, up to fifty years old, everyone who went in to serve and to work in the tent of testimony.
The total registered by their clans was two thousand two hundred fifty.
This was the registration of the clan of Kohath, everyone serving in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the Lord’s command through Moses.
The descendants of Gershon were registered by their ancestral households and their clans,
from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old, everyone who went in to perform their duties and do the work in the tent of testimony.
Their total registered by their clans and their ancestral households was two thousand six hundred thirty.
This was the registration of the clan of the descendants of Gershon, everyone serving in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the Lord’s command through Moses.
The clan of the descendants of Merari was also registered by their clans and their ancestral households.
From twenty years old and upward, up to fifty years old: everyone who enters service to perform the work of the tent of testimony.
Their total registered by their clans and their ancestral households was three thousand two hundred.
This was the registration of the clan of the descendants of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the Lord’s command through Moses.
Everyone who was registered, whom Moses and Aaron and the leaders of [?] registered among the Levites by their clans and their ancestral households,
From twenty years old and upward, up to fifty years old: everyone who enters to perform the work, according to the loads they carry in the tent of testimony.
those who were registered totaled eight thousand five hundred eighty.
At the Lord’s command through Moses, each man was registered according to his work and the things he carried. They were registered just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:
“Command the children of [?] to send outside the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone with a discharge, and everyone who is unclean because of a dead person.
You are to send them outside the camp, male and female alike, so that they do not defile their camps, where I dwell.”
The children of [?] did so and sent them outside the camp. Just as the Lord had spoken to Moses, so the children of [?] did.
And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:
“Speak to the children of [?], saying: If a man or woman commits any of the sins people commit, and through forgetfulness neglects him, and that person becomes guilty,
that person is to confess the sin they committed. They must repay the principal amount for their sin, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the person against whom they sinned.

But if the man has no close relative to receive restitution for his sin, his guilt payment shall belong to him; what he gives to the Lord shall belong to the priest, apart from the ram of atonement through which he will be forgiven.
And every first offering from all the things consecrated by the children of [?], which they bring to the Lord, shall belong to the priest.
Each person's consecrated things shall belong to him, and whatever a person gives to the priest shall belong to the priest.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Speak to the descendants of [?] and tell them: If any man’s wife transgresses and acts unfaithfully toward him,

And another man sleeps with her, having sexual intercourse with her, and she becomes defiled and hides it from her husband and receives him. She has been defiled, but no witness stands against her, and [?]
And jealousy comes over him, and he is jealous of his wife, although she has not been defiled.

The man shall bring his wife before the priest and present the offering on her behalf: a tenth of a measure of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, for it is an offering of jealousy, an offering of remembrance that brings a sin to mind.
And the priest shall bring her forward and make her stand before the Lord.
And the priest shall take holy, fresh water in an earthenware vessel. The priest shall take some dust from the ground where the tent of testimony stands and put it into the water.

And he shall make the woman stand before the Lord and uncover the woman's head. He shall place in her hand the offering of remembrance, the offering of jealousy. In the priest's hand shall be the water of reproof over which a curse will be pronounced.

And the priest shall put her under oath and say to the woman, “If no one has slept with you, and if you have not transgressed by defiling yourself while you have a husband, be unharmed by this water of reproof over which a curse is pronounced.
But if you have transgressed while you have a husband, or have been defiled, and someone other than your husband has had sexual intercourse with you—

The priest shall put the woman under oaths of cursing, and the priest shall say to the woman, “May the Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people, by making your thigh fall away and causing your belly to burn.
May this cursed water enter your belly, burning your abdomen and making your thigh fall away.” And the woman shall say, “So be it! So be it!”
And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the cursed water of reproof.
And he shall make the woman drink the water of reproof that is under the curse, and the cursed water of reproof shall enter her.
And the priest shall take the offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, lift the offering before the Lord, and bring it to the altar.
Then the priest shall take a handful from the offering as its memorial portion and offer it on the altar. After this, he shall make the woman drink the water.

And it shall happen that, if she has been defiled and has secretly concealed it from her husband, the cursed water of reproof shall enter her and burn her abdomen, and her thigh shall fall away. The woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman is pure and has not been defiled, she shall be unharmed and shall bear offspring.
This is the law of jealousy, when a woman transgresses it while she has a husband and becomes defiled,
or when jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. He shall make his wife stand before the Lord, and the priest shall carry out this entire law for her.
And the man shall be free from sin, but that woman shall bear her sin.
And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:
“Speak to the children of [?] and tell them: A man or woman who makes a special vow to consecrate themselves to the Lord

shall abstain from wine and strong drink. They must not drink wine or vinegar made from wine or vinegar made from strong drink. They must not drink anything made from grapes, and they must not eat fresh grapes or raisins.
Throughout all the days of his vow, he must eat nothing produced by the grapevine, from wine made from the dregs to grape wine and grape seeds.
Throughout all the days of his purification, no razor must touch his head. Until the days for which he made his vow are completed, he must remain holy, letting the hair of his head grow.
Throughout all the days of his vow to the Lord, he must not approach any dead person.
He must not defile himself for a father or mother, a brother or sister, if they die, because the vow to his God rests on him, upon his head.
Throughout all the days of his vow, he shall be holy to the Lord.
But if someone dies suddenly beside him and immediately defiles the head dedicated by his vow, he must shave his head on the day when he purifies himself. He must shave his head on the seventh day.
On the eighth day, he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of testimony.

The priest must offer one for sin and the other as a burnt offering. The priest must intercede for him, for his soul, because of the sins he committed, and they will be forgiven him. He must purify his head on that day.

This is the day on which he consecrated himself to the Lord by his vow. He must bring a year-old lamb for his guilt offering. The former days must not be counted, because the head dedicated by his vow was defiled.
This is the law for the person who has made a vow: on the day when he completes the days of his vow, he himself must bring his gift to the entrance of the tent.
He must offer it to the Lord: a year-old male lamb without blemish as a burnt offering, a year-old female lamb without blemish for sin, and a ram without blemish as a peace offering,
and a basket of unleavened bread made from fine flour, prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, together with their grain offering and their drink offering.
The priest must bring them before the Lord and offer what he gave for his sin, along with his burnt offering.
He must offer the ram as a peace sacrifice to the Lord, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest must also present its grain offering and its drink offering.
The person who made the vow must shave the head dedicated by his vow at the entrance of the tent of testimony. He must put the hair on the fire beneath the peace sacrifice.

The priest must take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hands of the person who made the vow, after he has shaved his head.

The priest must take them and set them before the Lord. They will be holy and belong to the priest, along with the breast of the lifted offering and the shoulder of the contribution. After this, the person who made the vow may drink wine.

This is the law for the person who has made a vow, who vows his offering to the Lord as part of his vow, besides whatever else he can afford. According to the extent of the vow he makes, he shall act in this way, according to the law of his purification.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and say: This is how you must bless the children of [?]. Say to them:
'May the Lord bless you and protect you.
May the Lord reveal his face to you and have mercy on you.
May the Lord lift up his face toward you and give you peace.'
They must place my name upon the children of [?], and I, the Lord, will bless them."
On the day when Moses finished setting up the tent, he anointed it and consecrated it together with all its equipment. He also anointed and consecrated the altar and all its equipment.
The leaders of [?] brought offerings—the twelve leaders of their ancestral households. These were the leaders of the tribes who were in charge of the census.
They brought their gift before the Lord: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, one wagon from every two leaders and one ox from each. They brought them before the tent.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Receive these from them so that they may be used for the work of serving the tent of testimony, and give them to the Levites, to each one according to his duties.”
And Moses took the carts and the cattle and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four cattle to the sons of Gershon according to their duties.
And he gave the four carts and the eight cattle to the sons of Merari according to their loads, under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
But he gave none to the sons of Kohath, because the service of the sanctuary was their responsibility, and they were to carry its things on their shoulders.
And the leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day when it was anointed. The leaders brought their gifts before the altar.
And the Lord said to Moses, “One leader each day shall take his turn; they shall present their gifts for the dedication of the altar.”
And on the first day, the one who brought his offering was Nahshon son of Amminadab, the leader of the tribe of Judah.

And he brought his gift: a silver basin for washing hands, weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and a silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour prepared with oil as a grain offering;
a bowl weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense;
a bull from the herd and a one-year-old lamb as a burnt offering;
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
and, as a peace offering, two cows, five rams, five goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the gift of Nahshon, the son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel, the son of Zuar, the leader of the tribe of Issachar, brought his offering.

And he brought his gift: a silver basin for washing hands, weighing one hundred thirty drachmas, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
a gold incense vessel weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense;
a bull from the herd, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb as a burnt offering;
and a goat from among the goats as a sin offering;
and, for the peace offering, two cows, five rams, five goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the gift of Nethanel, the son of Zuar.
On the third day, the leader of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab, the son of Helon.

His gift, which he brought, was a silver basin weighing one hundred thirty drachmas, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
a gold incense vessel weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense;
a bull from the herd, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb as a burnt offering;
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
and, for the peace offering, two cows, five rams, five goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the gift of Eliab, the son of Helon.
On the fourth day, the leader of the sons of Reuben, Elizur, the son of Shedeur.
He brought his gift: a silver basin weighing one hundred thirty drachmas, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as an offering, and a gold incense bowl weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a burnt offering.
And one male goat from the goats as a sin offering.
And as a peace offering, two heifers, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the gift of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day, the leader of the descendants of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

He brought his gift: a silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels and a silver bowl of [?] shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour prepared with oil as an offering.
A spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
And as a peace offering, two heifers, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the gift of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, the leader of the descendants of Gad, Eliasaph son of Reuel.

His gift was a silver dish for washing hands, weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both prepared with oil as an offering.
A spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
And as a sacrifice of well-being: two cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This is the offering of Eliasaph son of Reuel.
On the seventh day, the leader of the descendants of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud.

His offering was a silver washbasin weighing one hundred thirty shekels and a silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as an offering.
A spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
And as a peace offering, two heifers, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the gift of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day, the leader of the descendants of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

His gift was a silver dish for washing hands, weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour prepared with oil as an offering.
A spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull and one year-old lamb as a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
As a peace offering, two heifers, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the gift of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day, the leader of the descendants of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.

His offering was a silver washbasin weighing one hundred thirty shekels and a silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as an offering.
A spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
And for a peace offering: two cows, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day, the leader of the people of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

His offering was a silver washbasin weighing one hundred thirty shekels and a silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as an offering.
One gold spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull from the herd, one ram, and one one-year-old lamb, for a burnt offering.
One male goat from the flock of goats.
For a peace offering: two cows, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day, the leader of the descendants of Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran.

His offering was a silver basin for washing hands, weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both prepared with oil for an offering.
One gold spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull from the herd, one ram, and one one-year-old lamb, for a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
And for a peace offering: two cows, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.
On the twelfth day, the leader of the people of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.

His offering was a silver basin for washing hands, weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and a silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for an offering.
One gold spoon weighing ten gold pieces, filled with incense.
One young bull from the herd, one ram, and one one-year-old lamb, for a burnt offering.
One male goat from the herd as a sin offering.
And for a peace offering: two cows, five male goats, five rams, and five one-year-old lambs. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering for the altar on the day it was anointed, from the leaders of [?]: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold spoons.
Each dish weighed one hundred [?] shekels, and each bowl seventy shekels. All the silver in the vessels amounted to two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Twelve gold spoons filled with incense; all the gold in the spoons amounted to one hundred twenty gold pieces.

All the cattle for the burnt offering were twelve young bulls, twelve rams, and twelve one-year-old lambs, together with their grain offerings and their drink offering, and twelve male goats from the flock of goats for sin.

The cattle for the peace offering were twenty-four cows, sixty male goats, sixty rams, and sixty one-year-old lambs without any defect. This was the dedication offering for the altar after he had completed it with his own hand.

And after he had anointed it, as Moses was going into the tent of testimony to be spoken to, he heard the voice of the Lord speaking with him from above the atonement cover that was on the ark of testimony, between the two cherubim. And he spoke with him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Speak to Aaron and tell him, ‘You shall set the lamps on the right side, in front of the lampstand.’”
He lit the lamps just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And this was how the lampstand was made: it was cast gold, its shaft and its flower, solid throughout. He made the lampstand according to the pattern that the Lord had shown Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Take the Levites from among the children of [?] and purify them.”
And you shall do this for their purification: sprinkle them with the water of purification, and let a razor pass over his whole body. They shall wash their clothes and be clean.
And they shall take a young bull from the herd, and its offering shall be fine flour prepared with oil. You shall also take a young bull from the herd as a sin offering.
And you shall bring the Levites before the tent of testimony, and gather the entire assembly of the children of [?].
And you shall bring the Levites before the Lord, and the children of [?] shall lay their hands on the Levites.
And Aaron shall set apart the Levites as a gift before the Lord from the children of [?], so that they may perform the Lord’s work.
And the Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. He shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the Lord, to intercede for them and purify them.
And you shall place the Levites before Aaron the priest and before his sons, and present them as an offering before the Lord.
And you shall separate the Levites from among the children of [?], and they shall belong to me.
And afterward the Levites shall enter to work at the tent of testimony. You shall purify them and present them before the Lord.
As a gift, they are given from among the children of [?], in place of every firstborn among the children of [?].
From the firstborn among the children of [?], from humans to livestock, from the day when I struck every firstborn among them in the land of Egypt, I purified them for myself.
And they purified every firstborn.

I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the children of [?], to perform the work in the tent of testimony and to intercede for the children of [?], so that they may be forgiven. And no one from the children of [?] shall approach the holy things.
And Moses, Aaron, and the entire assembly of the children of [?] did this for the Levites. Just as the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did for them.
And the Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. Aaron presented them as an offering before the Lord and made an offering on their behalf to purify them.
And afterward the Levites entered to perform their service in the tent of testimony before Aaron and his sons. Just as the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so he did for them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
This is the rule for the Levites: from twenty-five years of age onward, they shall enter to serve in the tent of testimony.
And from fifty years of age, he shall withdraw from service and no longer work.
And his brother shall serve, keeping the duties in the tent of testimony, but he shall do no work. This is how you shall deal with the Levites regarding their duties.
And the Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt, saying:
Let the children of [?] observe the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, in the evening, you shall observe it at its appointed time. You shall observe it according to its laws and its rule.
And Moses spoke to the children of [?], telling them to observe the Passover.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, in the wilderness of Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, so the children of [?] did.
And the men who were unclean because of a human corpse came. They had been unable to celebrate the Passover on that day, and they came before Moses and Aaron that day.
And those men said to him, “We are unclean because of a dead person. So do not let us fall behind in bringing the Lord’s offering at its appointed time among the children of [?].”
And Moses said to them, “Stay here, so that I may hear what the Lord will command me concerning you.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Speak to the children of [?], saying: ‘Any person among you or your descendants who is unclean because of a human corpse or is on a distant journey shall observe the Lord’s Passover.
They shall observe it in the second month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must not leave any of it until morning, and they must not break a bone of it. They shall observe it according to the law of the Passover.

But if a person is clean and is not on a distant journey, yet neglects to observe the Passover, that person shall be cut off from their people, because they did not bring the Lord’s offering at its appointed time. That person shall bear their sin.

If a foreign resident comes to you in your land and observes the Lord’s Passover, he shall observe it according to the law of the Passover and its regulations. There shall be one law for you, for the foreign resident, and for the native of the land.’”
And on the day when the tent of testimony was set up, the cloud covered the tent, the house of testimony. In the evening it was over the tent like the appearance of fire, until morning.
This is how it always was: the cloud covered it by day, and there was an appearance of fire by night.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the children of [?] would then set out. And wherever the cloud stopped, the children of [?] would stop there.

At the Lord’s command the children of [?] would camp, and at the Lord’s command they would set out again. Throughout all the days when the cloud overshadowed the tent, the children of [?] would remain.
And whenever the cloud remained over the tent for many days, the children of [?] would keep watch for God and would not set out.
And whenever the cloud covered the tent for a few days, they would remain at the Lord’s word, and at the Lord’s command they would set out.
And whenever the cloud remained from evening until morning, or the cloud rose in the morning, they would set out, by day or by night.
Whether for a month or longer than a day, while the cloud overshadowed it, the children of [?] would remain and would not get up to set out.
For they traveled at the Lord’s command. They kept watch for the Lord according to the Lord’s order given through Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Make yourself two trumpets. You shall make them of hammered silver, and they shall be for you to summon the assembly and to have the camps set out.
You shall blow them, and the whole assembly shall gather at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
If you blow one, all the leaders of [?] shall come to you.
And you shall blow a signal, and the camps stationed toward the east shall set out.

And you shall sound a second trumpet signal, and the camps on the western side shall set out. And you shall sound a third trumpet signal, and the camps spread out by the sea shall set out. And you shall sound a fourth trumpet signal, and the camps stationed on the northern side shall set out. They shall sound a signal when they set out.
When you gather the assembly, you shall blow the trumpets, but not as a signal.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be a perpetual ordinance for you in your books.

When you go to war in your land against those who oppose you and rise up against you, you shall sound a signal with the trumpets, so that you may be remembered [?] before the Lord, and you shall be saved from the hands of your enemies.

And on your days of rejoicing, at your festivals, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow your trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of well-being. This shall be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.”
And in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud rose from above the tent of testimony.
The children of [?] set out, together with their possessions, from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud came to rest in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the Lord’s word given through Moses.
The division of the camp of Judah marched first with their army. Nahshon son of Amminadab was in command of their army.
Nethanel son of Zuar was in command of the army of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon was in command of the army of the tribe of Zebulun.
They will take down the tent, and the sons of Gideon and the sons of Merari will march, carrying the tent.
The division of the camp of Reuben marched with their army. Elizur son of Shedeur was in command of their army.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was in command of the army of the tribe of Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Reuel was in command of the army of the tribe of Gad.
The sons of Kohath will march, carrying the holy things. They will set up the tent before they arrive.
The division of the camp of Ephraim will march with their army. Elishama son of Ammihud was in command of their army.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was in command of the army of the tribe of Manasseh.
And the commander of the force of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
The division of the camp of the descendants of Dan will march last of all the camps, with their army. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was in command of their army.
Pagiel son of Ochran was in command of the army of the tribe of Asher.
Ahira son of Enan was in command of the army of the tribe of Naphtali.
These are the multitudes of the descendants of [?], and they marched with their army.

Moses said to Eliab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are going to the place of which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, because the Lord has spoken of good things for [?], to do it for him.”
He said to him, “I am coming, but I will go to my own land and my relatives.”
He said, “Do not leave us, because you were with us in the wilderness, and you became a representative among us.”
“If you come with us, and those good things that the Lord will give us come about, we will treat you well.”
They set out from the mountain of the Lord on a journey of three days. The ark of the Lord’s covenant went ahead of them on the three-day journey, looking for a resting place for them.
When the ark set out, Moses said, “Rise up, Lord! Let your enemies be scattered, and let everyone who hates you flee.”
At the resting place he said, “Return, Lord, to the thousands of tens of thousands among [?].”
Your cloud shaded them when they set out from the camp.
The people were grumbling about bad things before the Lord. The Lord heard and flew into a rage. Fire from the Lord blazed among them and consumed part of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire died down.
They called that place “Burning,” because a fire from the Lord had blazed among them.
And the mixed crowd among them began to crave food. They sat down and wept, and the children of [?] said, “Who will feed us meat?”
We remembered the fish we used to eat in Egypt, which we received for free, and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now our souls have dried up. We see nothing except this manna.
The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance was like the appearance of crystal.

The people would go out and gather it for themselves. They ground it in a mill or pounded it in a mortar, cooked it in a pot, and made it into cakes. Its taste was like the taste of a cake made with oil.
Whenever the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna came down on it.
Moses heard them weeping by their families, each one at his own doorway. The Lord became intensely angry, and the matter was evil.
And Moses said to the Lord, “Why have you mistreated your servant? Why have I not found favor in your sight, that you should place the burden of this people on me?”
Am I the father of all these people, or did I give birth to them, that you tell me, “Carry them in your arms, like a nurse who breastfeeds, into the land that I swore to their ancestors”?
Where will I find meat to give to all these people? They weep to me, saying, “Give us meat,” so that they can eat.
I cannot bear the burden of this people, because this task is too difficult for me.
If this is how you are going to treat me, kill me outright, if I have found favor with you, so that I will not see my suffering.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men from the elders of [?], men whom you know to be elders of the people and officers. Bring them to the tent of testimony, and let them stand there with you.”
I will speak with you there. I will take some of the [?] that is upon you and place it upon them. They will share with you the burden of this people, and you will not bear their burden alone.

And tell the people, “Purify yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, because you wept before the Lord, saying, ‘Who will feed us meat? We were better off in Egypt.’ The Lord will give you meat to eat, and you will eat meat.”
You will not eat it for just one day, or two, or five days, or twenty days.

You will eat it for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes bitter bile to you, because you have refused to trust the Lord who is among you. You wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”
And Moses said, “There are six hundred thousand men on foot among the people with whom I am, and you have said, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.’”
Will sheep and cattle be slaughtered for them, and [?] will they be enough for them? Or will all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, and will it not be enough for them?
And the Lord said to Moses, “Is the Lord’s hand not sufficient? Now you will know whether my word will come true for you or not.”
And Moses went in and spoke all the Lord’s words before the people. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

And the Lord came down in a cloud and spoke with him. He took some of the [?] that was upon him and placed it upon the seventy elders. When he placed the [?] upon them, they prophesied, but they did not continue.

Two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other was Medad. The [?] rested upon them. They were among those whose names had been recorded, but they had not come to the tent. Instead, they prophesied in the camp.
And a young man ran and reported to Moses, saying, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ chosen attendant, answered, “My lord Moses, stop them!”
And Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for me? Who will make all the Lord’s people prophets, when the Lord puts his [?] upon them?”
And Moses went into the camp, together with the elders of the people.

And a [?] came from the Lord and brought quail from the sea and cast them over the camp, a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on that side, all around the camp, two cubits above the ground.

And the people stayed up all that day, all that night, and all the next day, gathering the quail. Whoever gathered the least gathered ten cors, and they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
But the meat was still between their teeth, before they had chewed it, when the Lord became angry. And the Lord struck the people with a very great plague.
And they called that place “The Graves of Craving,” because there they buried the people who had craved.
And the people set out from the graves and traveled to Hazeroth, and the people stayed in Hazeroth.
And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married.
And they said, “Has the Lord spoken only with Moses? Has he not spoken with us too?” And the Lord heard.
Now the man Moses was very gentle, more than all the people living on the earth.
And the Lord spoke before Moses, saying to him, Aaron, and Miriam, “Go, all three of you, into the tent of testimony.” And the three of them went.
And the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance to the tent of testimony. And he called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them stood there.
And he said to them, “Listen to my words. If one of you becomes a prophet of the Lord, I will reveal myself to him in a vision, and I will speak with him in a dream.
It is not like this with my servant Moses. He is faithful in all my house.
I will speak with him mouth to mouth, in a visible form and not through riddles. And he has seen the glory of the Lord. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”
And the Lord’s furious anger came upon them.
And the cloud withdrew from above the tent. And there was Miriam, leprous, white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam, and saw that she was leprous.
And Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not charge us with sin because we acted foolishly and sinned.
Do not let him become like death, or like a miscarried child coming out of its mother’s womb and eating half of her flesh.”
And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying, “God, I beg you, heal her!”
And the Lord said to Moses, “If her father had spat in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days outside the camp? And afterward she may come back in.”
She separated herself outside the camp for seven days, and afterward she was to come back in. And the people did not travel until Miriam was cleansed.
And afterward the people traveled from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Send men to explore the land of the Canaanites, which I am going to give to the children of [?] as a possession. Send one man from each tribe, according to the divisions of their ancestral families, each one a leader among them.”
Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the Lord’s command. All the men were leaders of the children of [?].
These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Joshua son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, from the descendants of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Asshur;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Machir;
From the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi.
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to explore the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
And Moses sent them to inspect the land of Canaan, and he said to them, “Go up into this wilderness and go up into the hill country.”
“See what the land is like, and whether the people living in it are strong or weak, few or many.
See what the land they live in is like, whether it is good or bad, and what the cities they live in are like, whether they have walls or not.

See what the land is like, whether it is fertile or barren, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be persistent, and take some of the fruit of the land.” It was summer, the season when the grapes first ripen.
They went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, on the way into [?].
They went up into the wilderness and came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the giants descended from Anak, were there. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.

They came to the Valley of the Cluster and explored it. There they cut off a branch with a cluster of grapes on it and carried it on a pole. They also took some pomegranates from the pomegranate trees and some figs from the fig trees.
They called that valley the Valley of the Cluster because of the cluster that the children of [?] cut off there.
After forty days, they returned from exploring the land.

They traveled back to Moses, Aaron, and the whole assembly of the children of [?], in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They gave their report to them and to the whole assembly, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They spoke to them, saying, “We went into the land to which you sent us. It is a land flowing with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
But the people living in it are fierce, and the cities have very high walls and are very large. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the land to the south. The Hittites, Hivites, and Amorites live in the hill country, and the Canaanites live beside the sea and along the Jordan.”
Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said to him, “No! We will certainly go up and take possession of it, because we can surely overcome them.”
But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not going up, because we cannot go up against that nation: it is stronger than we are.”
They spread fear about the land they had seen among the children of [?], saying, “The land we passed through to inspect is a land that devours its inhabitants.
All the people we saw in it are exceptionally tall. We also saw giants there. In their presence we were like grasshoppers, and we were just as small in their eyes.”
The whole assembly raised its voice and cried out, and the people wept all that night.
All the children of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole assembly said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we would die here in this wilderness!
Why is the Lord bringing us into this land to fall in battle, and for our wives and children to become plunder? It would be better for us now to return to Egypt.”
And they said to one another, “Let us ask for a leader to take us back to Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the children of [?].
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had inspected the land, tore their clothes.
They spoke before the whole assembly of the children of [?], saying, “The land we inspected is very, very good.
If the Lord is pleased with us, he will bring us into the land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
But do not turn away from the Lord. Do not be afraid of the people of the land, because they are food for us. Their time has run out, but the Lord is among us. Do not be afraid of them.”
The whole assembly said to stone them, and they threw stones at them. Then the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud over the tent to the children of [?].
The Lord said to Moses, “How long will this people provoke me? How long will you refuse to believe me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
I will strike them with death and destroy them, and I will make you and your father’s household into a great nation, much more numerous than the household.”
Moses said before the Lord, “Egypt will hear, because you brought this people up from among them by your power.

And everyone living in the land has heard that you, Lord, are among your people, and that you, Lord, appear to them face to face. Your cloud has stood over them, and you travel with them, going ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
And you will wipe out this people as though they were one person. The nations that have heard of your name will say,
‘Because the Lord was unable to bring this people into the land he swore to give them, he laid them low in the wilderness.’
Now let your power be exalted, Lord, just as you said when you declared,

‘The Lord is patient, abounding in mercy and truthful, forgiving sin, wrongdoing, and lawlessness. Yet he will certainly not acquit the guilty, and he will punish the fathers’ sins in their children down to the third and fourth generation.’
Just as you have forgiven them from Egypt until now.
The Lord said to Moses, “I will forgive them according to your word.
But as surely as I live, and my name lives, the glory of the Lord will fill the whole earth.
For all these people who see my glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness have tested me—this is the tenth time—and have not obeyed my voice.

They will not see the land I swore to give their fathers. But their children who are here with me, who do not know good from evil—all these innocent little children—to them I will give the land. But everyone who provoked me will not see it.”
But my servant Caleb, because a different [?] was in him and he followed me, I will bring him into the land he entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow, turn back and travel into the wilderness along the road to the Red Sea.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
“How long will this wicked assembly grumble before me? I have heard the grumbling that the children of [?] have directed against you.”
Tell them, ‘As I live, says the Lord, I will do to you just as you have spoken in my hearing.
Your corpses will fall in this wilderness, along with your entire numbered company—all those among you who were counted, twenty years old and above, who grumbled against me.
You yourselves will not enter the land over which I stretched out my hand, promising that you would live there, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And your children, whom you said would become plunder, I will bring into the land, and they will inherit the land.
But your corpses will fall in this wilderness.
For forty years, and they will bear the burden of your unfaithfulness until your corpses perish in the wilderness.
According to the number of days during which you inspected the land—forty days, one day for each year—you will bear your sins for forty years, and you will know the fury of my anger.
I, the Lord, have spoken. This is what I will do to this wicked assembly that has stood against me: in this wilderness they will perish, and there they will die.’
And the men whom Moses sent to inspect the land, when they returned, grumbled about the land before the assembly, spreading bad reports about the land.
The men who spoke evil about the land died by the plague before the Lord.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived among those men who had gone up to inspect the land.
And Moses spoke these words before all the children of [?], and the people mourned deeply.
And when they rose early in the morning, they went up to the top of the mountain, saying, ‘Here we are! We will go up to the place the Lord spoke of, because we have sinned.’
And Moses said, ‘Why are you disobeying the Lord’s word? This will not turn out well for you.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you. You will fall before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away, refusing to trust the Lord, the Lord will not be among you.’
But they stubbornly went up to the top of the mountain. The ark of the Lord’s covenant and Moses, however, did not move out of the camp.
And the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in the mountain came down, struck them, and crushed them as far as Hormah, driving them back to the camp.
And the Lord spoke to Moses:
‘Speak to the children of [?] and tell them: When you enter the land that is to be your dwelling place, which I am giving you,

you shall prepare whole burnt offerings, burnt sacrifices to fulfill a vow, [?] you will give it willingly at your festivals, and you will offer a pleasing fragrance to the Lord, whether one offers cattle or sheep.
The person presenting his gift shall bring as a sacrifice a tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a measure of oil.
And you shall pour out a quarter of a measure of wine as a drink offering over the burnt offering, over the sacrifice. You shall prepare this for each lamb.
And for the ram that you offer as a burnt offering for sacrifice, you shall prepare a grain offering of fine flour: two tenths of fine flour mixed with one third of a measure of oil.
And you shall offer one third of a measure of wine as a drink offering, as smoke with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
As for the cattle from which you prepare burnt offerings for sacrifice, to fulfill their vows or as peace offerings to the Lord,
he shall offer with the bull a grain offering of fine flour mixed with half a measure of oil,
and half a measure of wine as a drink offering, as an offering of produce, as smoke with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
You shall do this for each bull or each ram.
According to the number of animals that you prepare from the sheep or the goats, you shall likewise do this for each one, according to their number.
And everyone counted among you shall do it this way, presenting offerings of this kind as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

And if there is a foreign resident among you who settles among your families and brings an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, in the same manner that you offer it, this is how the congregation of the Lord shall offer it.
There shall be one law for you and the foreign resident who has joined you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the foreign resident be before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the children of [?] and tell them: When you enter the land that I will give you,
when you eat the bread of the land, you shall set apart a contribution for the Lord.
From the first portion of your food you shall set apart a loaf as a contribution to the Lord. As with the firstfruits from a threshing floor, so shall you set it apart.
You shall give the first portion of your dough to the Lord as a contribution throughout your generations.
But whenever you sin and fail to carry out all these commandments that the Lord spoke to Moses,
as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day when the Lord commanded them to you and afterward throughout your generations,

and if an unintentional offense occurs on the part of the congregation, the whole congregation shall take a bull from the herd without any defect and offer it as a whole burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, together with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the prescribed rule, and a male goat from the goats as a sin offering.

The priest shall pray on behalf of the whole congregation of the children of [?], and they shall be forgiven for their unintentional offenses, because they too have brought their gift as an offering to the Lord for their sins, before the Lord, for their unintentional offenses.
The whole congregation of the children of [?] shall be forgiven, together with the foreign resident who has joined you, because it was an unintentional offense that occurred among all the people.
But if a single person sins unintentionally, that person shall bring a female goat one year old as a sin offering.
The priest shall pray before the Lord on behalf of the person who sinned unintentionally, and that person shall be forgiven.
For the native of the land among the children of [?] and the foreign resident there, you shall have one law concerning those who sin unintentionally.
But the person who acts defiantly, whether a native of the land or a foreign resident, has provoked God. That person shall be cut off from their people,
because that person has despised the word of God and rejected his commandments. That person shall be utterly destroyed and shall remain accountable for their sin.
Now the children of [?] were in the wilderness, and they found a man on the Sabbath day.
They brought him before Moses and Aaron and before the whole congregation of the children of [?].
They put him in custody, for they had not yet decided what they would do to him.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “This man must be put to death. Let the whole congregation stone him with stones outside the camp.”
The whole congregation stoned him with stones outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses:
“Speak to the children of [?] and tell them to make tassels for themselves on the edges of their clothes. You are to put a blue cord on the tassels at the edges.

They are to be on the edges of your clothes so that you will see them and remember all the Lord’s commandments and do them. You must not turn back to the thoughts of your heart and your eyes, following them into sexual immorality.
Instead, remember to do all my commandments and be holy to your God,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.”
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, spoke, along with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, son of Reuben.
They stood before Moses with two hundred and fifty men from the children of Israel, leaders of the congregation and prominent men in their councils, men of renown.

They rose up against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “The whole congregation consists of holy people, and the Lord is among them. Why, then, have you raised yourselves above the Lord’s whole congregation?”
When Moses heard this, he fell on his face.
He spoke to Korah and the whole congregation, saying, “An inquiry was made; God knew those who belonged to him, and [?] the holy one. He brought them near to himself.
Do this, then: take censers for yourselves. And those whom he did not choose, he did not bring near to himself—Korah and his whole congregation.
Put fire and incense on them before the Lord tomorrow. The man whom the Lord chooses will be the holy one. Let this, then, be enough for you, sons of Levi.”

“Is it a small thing to you that the God of [?] separated you from the midst of the congregation of [?], bringing you near to himself to serve him in [?] the duties of the Lord’s tent, and setting you before the tent to serve him?
He brought you near to himself, together with all your brothers, the sons of Levi. Yet today you have all gathered together, seeking to exercise the priesthood.
You and your congregation have gathered against the Lord. As for Aaron, who is he that you grumble against him?”
Moses gave orders to summon Dathan son of Eliab, but they said, “We are not coming.
Is it a small thing that you brought us out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in this wilderness, that you also set yourself up as ruler over us?
Even if you had brought us into the land flowing with milk and honey and given us inheritances of fields and vineyards, would you have gouged out those men’s eyes? We will not come up.”
Moses became very angry and said to the Lord, “Do not pay attention to their sacrifice. I have not taken anything that any of them desired, nor have I mistreated any of them.”
And Moses said to Korah, “Purify your assembly, and be ready before the Lord tomorrow, you and they, together with Aaron.
Each of you must take his censer, put incense on it, and bring it before the Lord, each with his own censer—250 censers. You and Aaron must also each bring your own censer.”
And each took his censer. They put fire in them and placed incense on them. Moses and Aaron stood at the doors of the tent of testimony.
And Korah assembled his whole assembly against them at the doors of the tent of testimony. And the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole assembly.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Separate yourselves from the midst of this assembly, so that I may destroy them all at once.”
And they fell on their faces and said, “O God, God of the heavens and of all flesh, if one man has sinned, will the Lord’s anger come upon the whole assembly?”
And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:
“Speak to the assembly, saying, ‘Move away from around the assembly of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
And Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and all the elders of [?] went with him.
And he spoke to the assembly, saying, “Separate yourselves from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that belongs to them, lest you be destroyed with them in all their sins.”
And they moved away from around Korah’s tent. But Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the doors of the tent, together with their wives, their children, and their belongings.
And Moses said, “By this you will know that the Lord sent me to do all these things, and that they were not my own doing.
If these men die as everyone dies, and if they meet the fate that everyone meets, then it was not the Lord who sent me.

But the Lord will reveal this through a chasm [?], and the earth will open its mouth and swallow them, along with the houses, their tents, and everything that belongs to them. They will go down alive into the realm of the dead, and you will know that these men have provoked the Lord.”
When he had finished all these words, the earth split open beneath them.
It swallowed them, their houses, all their people who were with Korah, and their livestock.
They went down alive into the realm of the dead, together with their possessions and their livestock. And the earth closed over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly.
And all of [?] who were around them fled at the sound they made, saying, “The earth might swallow us!”
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed the 250 men who had offered incense.
The Lord spoke with Moses
and with Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest: “Take these bronze censers out from among those who were burned, and scatter this foreign fire out of them.
