For the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives have been made holy. Make them into hammered plates and fasten them to the altar, because they were brought before the Lord and so became holy. And they became a sign for the children of [?].”
And Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, took the bronze censers that those who were burned had brought. They made them into bronze plates and fastened them to the altar,

as a reminder to the children of [?], so that from that time onward no outsider who was not descended from Aaron would undertake to offer incense before the Lord, and so that they would not become like Korah and his company, just as the Lord had spoken through Moses.
And the next day the children of [?] complained against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You are the ones who killed the Lord’s people!”
And when the assembly gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of testimony. The cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
And Moses and Aaron went in before the tent of testimony.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
“Separate yourselves from the midst of this assembly, so that I may destroy them all at once.” And they fell facedown.

And Moses said to Aaron, “Take the censer, put fire from the altar on it, and put incense on it. Take it quickly into the camp and make an offering on their behalf, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord and has begun to strike the people.”
And Aaron took it as Moses had told him and ran to the assembly. The plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made an offering on behalf of the people.
And he stood between the living and the dead, and the plague stopped.
Those who died in the plague numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died because of Korah.
And Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and the plague had stopped.
And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:

“Speak to the children of [?] and take staffs from them, one staff for each ancestral household, from each of their leaders according to their ancestral households: twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
Of Levi [?], for they shall give only one staff for the tribe according to their ancestral households.
And you shall place them in the tent of testimony, before the testimony. Among these I will reveal myself to you in that place.
And the staff of the man whom I choose will sprout. I will remove from you the grumbling of the children of [?], which they direct against you.”
And Moses spoke to the children of [?], and all their leaders gave him a staff, one staff for each leader according to their ancestral households: twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among the staffs.
And Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the tent of testimony.
And on the next day Moses and Aaron went into the tent of testimony. Look! Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted. It had put out a shoot, produced flowers, and borne nuts.
And Moses brought out all the staffs from before the Lord to all the children of [?]. They looked at them, and each man took his staff.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Place Aaron’s staff before the testimonies, to be kept as a sign for the disobedient children, so that their grumbling against me may stop and they may not die.”
And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded Moses. That is what they did.
And the children of [?] spoke to Moses, saying, “Look! We have perished, we have been destroyed, we have been scattered.
Everyone who touches the Lord’s tent dies. Are we to [?] die to the last person?”

The Lord spoke to Aaron, saying, “You and your sons and your ancestral household shall bear the sins connected with the holy things. You and your sons shall bear the sins connected with your priesthood.
Bring your brothers, the tribe of Levi, your father’s people, close to you. Let them join you and serve you, while you and your sons with you are before the tent of testimony.
They shall carry out your duties and the duties of the tent. But they must not approach the sacred utensils or the altar, so that neither they nor you die.
Let them join you and carry out the duties of the tent of testimony, performing every service of the tent. But an outsider must not come near you.
And you shall carry out the duties of the holy things and the duties of the altar, so that wrath may not arise again among the children of [?].
I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the children of [?] as a gift to the Lord, to perform the services of the tent of testimony.

You and your sons with you must guard your priesthood in everything concerning the altar and what is inside the curtain. You must perform the duties of your priesthood, given as a gift. Any outsider who approaches these things must die.

And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying, “Look, I have given you responsibility for my firstfruits, from everything that the children of [?] have consecrated to me. I have given them to you as an honor, and to your children after you, as a lasting ordinance.”

This shall be yours from the holy offerings that have been consecrated: all their gifts, all their sacrifices, all their atonement offerings, and all their sin offerings. Whatever they give me from all these holy things shall belong to you and your sons.
You shall eat them in the most holy place. Every male may eat them—you and your sons. They shall be holy to you.

You shall also have the firstfruits of their gifts of honor, from what the children of [?] offer up. I have given them to you and your sons with you as a permanent provision. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
All the firstfruits of oil and all the firstfruits of wine and grain—the firstfruits they give to the Lord—I have given to you.
All the first produce of their land that they bring to the Lord shall belong to you. Everyone in your household who is clean [?]; you shall eat them.
Everything devoted to God among the children of [?] shall belong to you.

Every [?] from all flesh that they offer up to the Lord, from humans to livestock, shall belong to you. But the firstborn of humans must be redeemed, and you must receive a redemption payment for the firstborn of unclean animals.
The redemption payment, from the age of one month, shall be five shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty obols. They shall belong to me.

But no redemption payment shall be received for the firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats. They are holy. You must pour their blood all around the altar and offer up the fat as an offering, a pleasing fragrance to the Lord.
Their [?] shall belong to you, just as the breast of the raised offering and the right shoulder belong to you.

Everything from the holy things that the children of [?] set apart to give to the Lord, I have given to you, your sons, and your daughters with you as a permanent provision. It is an everlasting covenant of [?] before the Lord, for you and your descendants after you.
The Lord spoke to Aaron, saying to him, “You shall not inherit any of their land, nor shall you have a share among them, because I am your share and your inheritance among the children of [?].”
“As for the sons of Levi, look, I have given them the tithes of the children of [?] as an inheritance, in return for the duties they perform in the service of the tent of testimony.
From now on, the children of [?] must not approach the tent of testimony and incur sin.

The Levite shall perform the service of the tent of testimony, and they shall bear their sins. This is a lasting ordinance throughout their generations, and they shall receive no inheritance among the children of [?].

For the tithes of the children of [?], which they set apart as an offering to the Lord, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance. That is why I told them, ‘They shall not receive an inheritance among the children of [?].’”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“You shall also speak to the Levites and say to them, ‘When you receive from the children of [?] the tithe that I have given you from them as your allotted share, you yourselves shall set aside an offering from it for the Lord, a tenth of the tithe.’”
“Your offerings that are set apart shall be counted for you as grain from a threshing floor and as what is drawn from a winepress.
You yourselves must likewise set apart the Lord’s offerings from all the tithes you receive from the children of [?]. From them you must give the Lord’s firstfruits to Aaron the priest.
From everything given to you, you must take out a firstfruit offering to give to the Lord, or, from every firstfruit offering, what has been consecrated from it.
You shall tell them, ‘When you take the firstfruit offering out of it, it shall be counted for the Levites as produce from a threshing floor and as produce from a winepress.
You and your children may eat it anywhere, because it is your payment in return for your duties in the tent of testimony.’
You will not incur sin because of it when you take its firstfruits from it. You must not defile the holy things of the Israelites, so that you do not die.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
“This is the ordinance of the law that the Lord commanded, saying: Speak to the Israelites, and have them bring you a clean red heifer with no defect, on which no yoke has been placed.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. They must take it outside the camp to a clean place and slaughter it before him.
Eleazar must take some of its blood and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the tent of testimony seven times.
They must burn its blood and its dung.
The priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop, and they shall throw them into the fire burning the heifer.
The priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest will remain unclean until evening.
The person who burns it must also wash his clothes and bathe his body in [?]. He will remain unclean until evening.

And a clean man shall gather the ashes of the heifer and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the assembly of the children of [?], to make water for sprinkling with which they shall be purified.
The person who gathers the heifer’s ashes must wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This will be a lasting ordinance for the Israelites and the converts who settle among you.
Whoever touches the body of any dead person will be unclean for seven days.
He must purify himself on the third day and the seventh day, and he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and the seventh day, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a dead person, a human being, and does not purify himself has defiled the Lord’s tent. That person must be cut off from his people, because the water for sprinkling has not been sprinkled on him [?]. He is unclean; his uncleanness remains in him.
This is the law: If someone dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house will be unclean for seven days.
Every open container that has not been secured with a fastening is unclean.
Anyone who touches a slain person or a corpse, a human bone or a grave, out in the open field, will be unclean for seven days.

They must take some of the ashes of the purification offering that was burned, for seven days. They must take some of the ashes of the purification offering that was burned and pour fresh water over them in a container.

A clean person must take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the unclean person, the house, the utensils, and the people who are there, and on the person who touched human earth [?], or the slain person in the house who died [?], or the grave.

The clean person must exercise power over the unclean person on the third day and the seventh day. He will be clean on the seventh day. He must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.

Anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify himself must be cut off from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the Lord’s holy things. Because the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean.
This will be a lasting ordinance for you. The person who sprinkles the water for sprinkling must wash his clothes, and anyone who touches the water for sprinkling will remain unclean until evening.
Everything the unclean person touches will be unclean, and anyone who touches the unclean person will remain unclean until evening.”
The Israelites and the whole congregation came [?] to the wilderness of Sinai in the first month. The people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the assembly, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people cursed Moses, saying, “It would have been better if we had died when our brothers perished before the Lord.
Why did you bring the Lord’s congregation into this desert to kill us, our children, and our livestock?

What was the benefit of bringing us out of Egypt to make us come to this terrible place? What is this place? It is not sown, and there are no fig trees, grapevines, or pomegranate trees. There is not even water for us to drink.”
Moses and Aaron came from before the assembly to the entrance of the tent of testimony and fell facedown. The glory of the Lord appeared to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Take the staff and gather the assembly, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before them, and it will give its water, so that you can give the assembly and their livestock water to drink.”
Moses took the staff that was before the Lord, as the Lord had said.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock, and he said to them, “Listen to me, you disobedient people! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with the staff. A great deal of water came out, and the assembly and their livestock drank.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust me and show my holiness before the children of [?], you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”
This is the water of dispute, because the children of [?] spoke against the Lord, and he showed his holiness among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying, “This is what your brother [?] says: You know all the suffering that has come upon us,
from the time our ancestors went down to Egypt and lived as Egyptians in Egypt for many days. The Egyptians oppressed us and our ancestors.
We cried out to the Lord, and the Lord heard our voice. He sent an angel from heaven, and they brought us out of Egypt. Now we are in Kadesh, a city in a district within your borders.

We are coming through your land. We will not go through your fields or your vineyards, nor will we drink water from your well. We will travel on the king’s road and will not turn to the right or the left until we have passed through your territory.”
The king of Edom said to them, “You cannot pass through my territory. Otherwise, we will come out to fight against you in war.”

The children of [?] said to him, “We will travel alongside the water until we have passed you. If we and our livestock drink any of your water, we will give you its [?]. But this is nothing: we will travel along the foot of the mountain until we have passed you.”
But he said, “You will not be able to pass through my territory.” The king of Edom came out to confront them with a great multitude and a powerful force.
The king of Edom refused to allow [?] to pass through his territory, so [?] turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the children of [?], the whole assembly, came up to Mount Hor.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron on Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, saying:
“Look, Aaron will be gathered to his people, for you will not enter the land that I gave your ancestors, because you treated me with contempt at the water of the dispute.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up onto Mount Hor before the whole assembly.
Strip Aaron of his robe and put it on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered and will die there.”
Moses did as the Lord had commanded him. He brought him up onto the mountain before the whole assembly.
He stripped him of his clothes and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died on the summit of the mountain, and Moses came down from the mountain with Eleazar.
The whole assembly saw that they had left Aaron behind. The entire house of [?] wept for Aaron for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the wilderness, heard that [?] had come by the road of Atharim. He fought against [?] and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow, saying, “If the Lord gives this people into my hands, I will destroy them and their city.”
The Lord heard the voice of [?] and delivered the Canaanite into his hands. He devoted him and his city to destruction, and they called that place “Destruction.”
They set out from Mount Hor along the road leading toward the sea, going around the land of Edom. The people grew discouraged along the way.
The people spoke against Moses, saying, “Why have you brought us out of Egypt to kill us in the wilderness? We have neither bread nor water, and we hate this worthless bread.”
The Lord sent deadly snakes among the people. They bit the people, and a great many of the children of [?] died.

The people came to Moses, saying, “We have sinned. We have spoken against God and against you. Now plead with the Lord for us, so that he will take these snakes away from us.” Moses pleaded with the Lord for the people.
The Lord said to Moses, “Make a bronze snake and put it on a pole. Whenever a snake bites someone, let everyone bitten by the snakes look at it and live.”
Moses made the bronze snake and set it upright on a pole. Whenever a snake bit someone and that person looked at the bronze snake, he lived.
The children of [?] set out from that place and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the edge of the wilderness facing Moab, toward the sunrise.
They set out from that place and camped in the valley of Zered.

They set out from that place and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends beyond the territory of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the boundary of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
For this reason they say in the book, “The Lord’s war burned Moab and the torrent of Arnon,
and he established the torrents for Ar to dwell among them, which is near the border of Moab.”
The well was in that place. This is the well about which the Lord said to Moses, “Gather the people around it, and I will give them water to drink.”
Then [?] sang a song over the well: “Come out, all of you, to
the well. The rulers dug it. The kings dug it among the nations, in their kingship, when they ruled over them. From the well until you come up.”
To Enathanaen [?], and from Enathanaein [?], until you come up to Manael [?], until you come up to Manamoth [?].
And from Bamoth until you come up to the summit of the carved rock, which overlooks the wilderness.
From that place Moses sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, with peaceful words, saying,

“We will pass through your land, traveling along the road. We will not turn aside into fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from your well. We will travel along the king’s highway until we have crossed your borders.”
Sihon did not allow [?] to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people and went out into the wilderness to fight against [?]. He came to Jahaz and drew up his battle line against [?].
But God struck him down with the sword and ruled over his people, from Arnon to Jabbok and as far as the children of Ammon, because Jazer was within the territory of the children of Ammon.
[?] took all these cities and lived in all the cities of the Amorites.
This man had previously fought against the king of Moab and taken all his land, from Aroer to Arnon.
For this reason those who recite these riddles say, “Come into Heshbon, so that it may be built and the city of Sihon established.
For fire came out of Heshbon, and a flame from the city of Sihon. It devoured as far as Moab and swallowed up the pillar of Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have been destroyed. They handed over their sons to escape and their daughters as captives to Sihon, king of the Amorites.”
Their descendants will perish, from Heshbon down to Dibon, and their women kindled a fire against Moab.
But [?] lived in all the cities of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to scout out Jazer. He captured it and its towns and drove out the Amorite who lived there.
Then they turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet them at Edrei, together with all his people.

The Lord said to Moses, “Do not be afraid of him, because I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and all his land. Do to him as you did to the king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon.”
He struck down him, his sons, and all his people, until no one breathing was left among them. He took possession of their land.
Then the children of [?] set out from there and camped in the camping grounds of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything that [?] had done to the Amorites.
Moab was afraid of the Lord’s people, because they were very numerous. Moab was deeply troubled in the presence of the children of [?].
Moab said to the whole council of elders of Midian, “Now these people will devour us and everyone around us, just as a calf eats [?] in the field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at [?], which is beside the river in the land of the children of his people, to summon him, saying, “Look, a people has come out of Egypt. They have covered the face of the land and have settled near me.

Now come and curse these people for me, because they are stronger than we are. Perhaps we will be able to strike down some of them and drive them out of our land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse will be under a curse.”
All the elders of Moab went with the elders of Midian, carrying their divination equipment in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak’s words.
Balaam said to them, “Stay here with me tonight, and I will tell you what the Lord says to me.” So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said to him, “What are these men doing with you?”
Balaam said, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent them to me, saying,

‘Look, a people has come out of Egypt. They have covered the face of the land and have settled near me. Now come and curse these people for me, so that I may see whether I can defeat them and drive them out of my land.’”
God said to Balaam, “You must not go there, nor must you curse these people, because they are blessed.”
Abraham rose early and said to Balak’s officials, “Go back to your master. God has not permitted me to come with you.”
The officials of Moab set out and came to Balak. They said to him, “Balaam did not want to come with us.”
Balak again sent other officials, more numerous and more distinguished than these.
They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘I beg you, do not hesitate to come to me,
for I will honor you greatly, and whatever you ask for, I will give you.’”
Balaam answered Balak’s officials, “Even if Balak gives me his entire house filled with gold and silver, I cannot disobey the Lord’s word by doing anything small or great on my own initiative.
Now you too must stay here with me this other night, so that I may learn what else the Lord will say to me.”
God came to Balaam during the night and said to him, “If these men have come to summon you, get up and follow them. But you must do only what I tell you.”
Balaam rose early, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
The angel of the Lord rose and came out of heaven to cast him down. He was riding his donkey, with his two servants accompanying him.

When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord standing on the road with his sword drawn in his hand, she turned off the road and went into the field. He struck her with his staff to bring her back onto the road.
The angel of the Lord stood between the vineyard paths, with a wall on this side of him and a wall on the other side.
When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she pressed herself against the wall and crushed Balaam’s foot. Balaam struck her again.
The angel of the Lord went farther and stood in a narrow place where it was impossible to turn to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she lay down under Balaam. Balaam became angry and struck the donkey with his staff.
God opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you? This is the third time you have struck me.”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have caused me trouble. If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, whom you have ridden from your youth until today? Have I ever neglected you and done this to you?” He said, “No.”
God revealed it to Balaam, and he saw the angel of God standing in the middle of the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He fell on his face and bowed down.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey? This is the third time. Look, I have come down to stop you, because your way is not right before me.
When the donkey saw me, she turned away from me. This is the third time. If she had not turned away, I would now have killed you, but I would have kept the donkey alive.”
Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, “I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing against me on the road to meet me. Now, if this action does not please you, I will turn back.”
The angel of God said to Balaam, “Go with these men. But be careful to say only the words I tell you.” Balaam went with Balak’s officials.
When Balak heard that Balaam had arrived, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not send for you and call you? Why did you not come to me? If I really could not honor you, I would not have sent for you.”
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. But can I now say anything at all? I will say only the words God puts in my mouth.”
Abraham went with Balak and came to the city of Nersoue.
Balak slaughtered sheep and cattle and sent them to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
When morning came, Balak took Balaam and brought him up onto the pillar of Baal. From there he showed him a part of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam had told him and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.

Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your sacrifice, and I will go and see whether God will appear to me as I go to meet him. Whatever words he speaks to me, I will tell you.” Balak stood beside his sacrifice. Balaam went toward the Lord [?], and he went straight ahead.
God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to him, “Look, I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on the altar.”
God put words into Balaam’s mouth and said to him,
“Return to Balak and speak to him in this way.”

He returned to him and found him standing beside his burnt offerings, with all the officials of Moab with him. The [?] of God came upon him, and he spoke his oracle, saying, “Balak, the king of Moab, sent for me from Mesopotamia. He sent from the mountains of the east, saying, ‘Come, curse Jacob for me, and curse [?].’
“How can I curse someone God has not cursed? Or why should I revile someone God has not reviled?
“For from the mountain tops I will look at him, and the hills will take care of him. Look, here is a people who will dwell alone, and what nation will be like them?”
Who has come from your offspring, Jacob? Or who will count [?] the peoples of [?]? Let my soul die among the souls of the righteous, and let my offspring be like their offspring.
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I called you to curse my enemies, and look, you are blessing them!”
Balaam said to Balak, “What have I done to you? Did I not tell you that whatever God puts into my mouth, I will be compelled to say?”

Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you will not see the people there, but will see only a portion of them. You will not see all the people. Curse them for me from that place.”
He took him to the top of the hewn mountain, to the lookout over the field. He built seven altars there and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your sacrifice. I will go to God.”
He met Balaam, put a word into his mouth, and said to him, “Return to Balak and say these things to him.”
They brought him back to him. He was standing beside his burnt offering, with all the rulers of Moab. Balak said to him, “What did the Lord say to you?”
He spoke his oracle and said, “Rise, Balak, and listen! Hear me, witness, son of Zippor!
God is not like a human being, to be judged, nor like a human child, for people to be angry with him. He has spoken; will he not act? Will he speak and not carry it through?
Look, I have been brought here to bless. I will bless and will not turn back.
There will be no suffering in Jacob, nor will trouble appear in [?], because the Lord God is with him. The glories of rulers are within him, for
God is the one who brought them out of Egypt. He has glory like that of a unicorn.
For there is no diviner in Jacob, nor any instruments of divination in [?]. At their proper time they will speak in Jacob and [?].
Look, a people will rise like lion cubs and lift themselves up like lions. They will not sleep until they have eaten prey, and they will drink the blood of the slain.”
Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them for me at all, and do not bless them at all!”
Balaam answered and said to Balak, “Did I not speak to you and say, ‘Whatever God tells me, I will do’?”
Balak said to Balaam, “Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God, and you will curse them for me from there.”
Balak took Balaam to the summit of Peor, which faces the wilderness.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam had told him, and he offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
Balaam saw that blessing [?] was pleasing to the Lord. He did not go, as was his custom, to meet him through divination, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam raised his eyes and saw [?] moving by tribes, and the [?] of God came upon him.
They took up his oracle. Balaam son of Beor said, “The man whose eyes are truly open says:
The one who saw the vision of God in a trance, with his eyes uncovered.
How beautiful are your houses, Jacob, and your tents, [?]!
Like shady valleys, like gardens beside rivers, like tents that God has pitched, and like cedars beside the waters.
A man will come from his offspring and rule over many nations. He will be exalted above the kingdom of Gog, and his kingdom will grow.

For God is the one who led him as he came out of Egypt. He has glory like that of a unicorn. He will devour the nations along with their strength, and he will also devour their backs and their bones. He will pierce his enemy with his arrows.
He lay down and rested like lions. Who can rouse him? Those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed.

Balak became angry with Balaam and struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not call you to curse my enemy for me? But look, you have blessed him with a blessing! This is the third time!
Now go back to your own place. I had said, ‘I will honor you,’ but now God has deprived you of honor.”
When Balaam and Balak had said these things, Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not tell your messengers whom you sent to me,
‘Even if Balak gives me his whole house filled with gold and silver, I cannot transgress the Lord’s word to do anything bad or good on my own’?
What God tells me is what I will say. Now I will return to my place. Come, let me advise you about what this people will do to your people in the last days.
He returned to his oracle and said, “Balaam son of Beor speaks; the man who sees truly speaks,
who hears the words of God, who sets forth instruction from the Most High, who sees a vision of God in sleep, with his eyes uncovered.

I will proclaim him, and now I will bless again, and he will not draw near. A star will rise from Jacob, and a man will arise from [?]. He will crush the leaders of Moab; he will plunder all the sons of Seth.
Edom will become a possession, and Esau, his enemy, will become a possession. But [?] rose up in strength.
He will arise from Jacob and destroy whoever escapes from the city.”
When he saw Amalek, he returned to his oracle and said, “Amalek is the first of the nations; his descendants will perish.”
When he saw the Kenite, he returned to his oracle and said, “Your dwelling place is strong, and if you place your children in a rock—
And if the sons of a crafty man become Beor [?], the Assyrians will take you captive.
He returned again to his oracle and said, “Oh, who will survive if God allows these things?
He will come from the hands of [?], and they will humble the Assyrians. They will afflict the Hebrews, and they too will perish together.”
Balaam got up, went away, and returned to his own place. Balak also returned to his home.
And [?] settled in Shittim. The people defiled themselves by having illicit sex with the daughters of Moab.
They invited them to the sacrifices offered to their idols. The people ate from their sacrifices and worshiped their idols.
And [?] served Baal-peor, and the Lord became fiercely angry with [?].
The Lord said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and make a public example of them before the Lord in the sunlight.
Then the fierce anger will turn away from [?].” Moses said to the tribes of [?], “Let each one kill the member of his household who served Baal-peor.”

And look, a man from among the sons of [?] came and brought his brother with a woman from Midian, before Moses and before the whole assembly of the sons of [?]. They were weeping at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the midst of the assembly and took a spear in his hand.
He went into the chamber after the Israelite man and pierced both of them—the Israelite man and the woman—through her belly. Then the wrath ceased among the sons of [?].
Those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, is the one who turned away my anger from the children of [?], when they were zealous with my zeal among them. And I did not destroy the children of [?] in my zeal.
Tell him, ‘Look, I will give him a covenant of peace.
It will be a covenant of everlasting priesthood for him and his descendants after him, because he [?] for his God and pleaded on behalf of the children of [?].’”
The name of the Israelite man whom he struck down with the woman from Midian was Zimri, the son of Salu, the leader of a family household of Simeon.
And the name of the woman from Midian whom he struck down was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, the leader of the nation of Omoth, a family household in Midian.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Speak to the children of [?], saying:”
“Treat the Midianites as enemies and strike them down,

because they are acting as your enemies through deceit. They are deceiving you in the matter of Peor and of Cozbi, the daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague because of Peor.”
After the plague, the Lord spoke to Moses and Eleazar the priest, saying,
“Take a count of the whole congregation of the children of [?], from twenty years old, according to their family households—everyone among the children of [?] who goes out to war.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest took a count on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
“Count those twenty years old and above,” as the Lord had told Moses and the children of [?] who came out of Egypt.
Reuben was the firstborn of [?]. The sons of Reuben were Hanoch—and the clan of Hanoch was the Palluites; the clan of Pallu was the Palluites.
The clan of Hezron was the Hezronites; the clan of Carmi was the Carmites.
These are the clans of Reuben, and their number amounts to forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty.
And the son of Pallu was Eliab.
The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were the leaders of the assembly when they rose up against the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and the congregation, when the fire consumed the two hundred and fifty. They became a sign.
None of the sons of Korah died.
And the sons of Simeon—the clans of the sons of Simeon: the clan of Nemuel was the Nemuelites; the clan of Jamin was the Jaminites; the clan of Jachin was the Jachinites.
The clan of Zerah was the Zerahites; the clan of Shaul was the Shaulites.
These were the clans of Simeon. According to their census, they numbered twenty-two thousand.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The sons of Judah according to their clans: the clan of Shelah was the Shelanites; the clan of Perez was the Perezites; the clan of Zerah was the Zerahites.
And the sons of Perez formed the clan of Hezron; the clan of Hamul was the Hamulites.
These were the clans of Judah. According to their census, they numbered seventy-six thousand five hundred.
And the sons of Issachar according to their clans: the clan of Tola was the Tolaites; the clan of Puvah was the Puvahites.
The clan of Jashub is the Jashubites. The clan of Shimron is the Shimronites.
These are the clans of Issachar. According to their census, they number 64,300.
And the sons of Zebulun according to their clans: the clan of Sered is the Seredites; the clan of Elon is the Elonites; the clan of Jahleel is the Jahleelites.
These are the clans of Zebulun. According to their census, they number 5,500.
And the sons of Gad according to their clans: the clan of Zephon is the Zephonites; the clan of Haggi is the Haggites; the clan of Shuni is the Shunites.
The clan of Ozni is the Oznites; the clan of Eri is the Erites.
The clan of Allon is the Allonites. The clan of Ariel is the Arielites.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad. According to their census, they number 44,500.
And the sons of Asher according to their clans: the clan of Jamin is the Jaminites; the clan of Ishvi is the Ishvites; the clan of Barta is the Bartaites.
The clan of Heber is the Heberites. The clan of Malchiel is the Malchielites.
And the name of Asher’s daughter is Sarah.
These are the clans of Asher. According to their census, they number 43,600.
And the sons of Joseph according to their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
And the sons of Manasseh: the clan of Machir is the Machirites. And Machir fathered Gilead.
The clan of Gilead. The clan of Ahiezer is the Ahiezerites. The clan of Helek is the Helekites.
The clan of Asriel is the Asrielites. The clan of Seyim [?] is the Shechemites.
The clan of Sumael is the Sumaelites. The clan of Hepher is the Hepherites.
The clan of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher: no son was born to him, but there were children. And the names of Zelophehad’s children are Maada, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh. According to their census, they number 52,700.
And these are the sons of Edam: the clan of Shuthelah is the Shuthelahites; the clan of Tahan is the Tahanites.
These are the sons of Shuthelah: the clan of Edom is the Edomites.
These are the clans of Naphtali. According to their census, they number 32,500. These are the clans of Joseph according to their clans.
And the sons of Benjamin according to their clans: the clan of Bari is the Baraites; the clan of Ahiram is the Ahiramites.
The clan of Sophan is the Sophanites.
And the sons of Warad are the Baradites and Naaman. The clan of Ard is the Ardites. The clan of Naaman is the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin according to their clans. According to their census, they number 35,500.
The sons of Dan according to their clans: the clan of Shuham is the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan according to their clans.
All the clans of Shimei, according to their census, totaled sixty-four thousand six hundred.
And the descendants of Naphtali, according to their clans: the Asherite clan of Asher;
the Gunite clan of Guni; the Jezerite clan of Jezer; the Shillemite clan of Shillem.
These are the clans of the descendants of Naphtali. According to their census, they totaled forty-three thousand three hundred.
This is the count of the children of [?]: six hundred thousand seven hundred thirty.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
You shall divide the land among these people for them to inherit it, according to the number of their names.
You shall increase their inheritance for them, and you shall give those who are fewer their inheritance. You shall give each one their inheritance according to the census you took of them.
You shall divide the land by lots. They shall inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes, by lot.
You shall divide their inheritance among the many and the few.
And the descendants of Levi, according to their clans: the Gideonite clan of Gideon; the Gathonite clan of Gathon; the Merarite clan of Merari.
These are the clans of the sons of Levi: the clan of Libni, the clan of Hebron, the clan of Korah, and the clan of Mushi. Kohath fathered Amram.
His wife's name was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, whom [?] bore to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam to Amram.
To Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they brought unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
According to their census, they totaled twenty-three thousand, counting every male one month old and older. They were not counted among the children of [?].
This is the census of Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the children of [?] in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Among these there was not a single person from those counted by Moses and Aaron, who had counted the children of [?] in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the Lord had told them, “They will certainly die in the wilderness.” Not one of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The children of Zelophehad son of Ophir, son of Arad, son of Machir, from the descendants of Manasseh, the descendants of Joseph, came forward. These were their names: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses and Eleazar the priest, before the leaders and the whole congregation, at the entrance to the tent of testimony, and said:
“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the congregation that rebelled before the Lord, in the whole congregation of Korah. He died because of his own sin, and he had no son.
So do not let our father's name disappear from his clan because he has no son. Give us, too, a property among our father's brothers.”
Moses brought their case before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“The children of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall give them a hereditary possession among their father’s brothers and assign their father’s allotted inheritance to them.”
“You shall speak to the children of [?], saying: If a man dies without a son, you shall transfer the inheritance to his daughter.
But if he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to the brother [?].
[?] of his father.

But if his father has no brother, you shall give his inheritance to his nearest relative in the tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a legal statute for the Israelites, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Go up onto the mountain at the edge, namely Mount Nebo, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am going to give the Israelites as a possession.
When you have seen it, you too shall be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron was gathered on Mount Hor.

For you disobeyed my command in the wilderness of Sinai when the assembly opposed me. You were to show my holiness, but you did not show my holiness at the water before them. This is the water of dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Sinai.”
Moses said to the Lord:
“May the Lord, the God of [?] and the authorities and all flesh, appoint a man over the assembly,”
“who goes out before them, who will lead them out and bring them in again, so that the Lord’s assembly will not be like sheep that have no shepherd.”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Bring Joshua son of Nun to you, a man who has [?] within him, and lay your hands on him.”
“Let him present him before Eleazar the priest, and give him instructions before the whole assembly. And instruct them concerning him in their presence.
And you shall give him some of your authority, so that the Israelites will obey him.

And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and they shall consult him about the revealed decision before the Lord. At the command of his mouth they shall go out, and at the command of his mouth they shall come in again—he, the Israelites, and the whole assembly.”
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and presented him before Eleazar the priest and before the whole assembly.
And he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Command the Israelites and tell them: My gifts, my offerings of honor, my offerings of produce as a pleasing aroma, which you shall offer to me at my festivals.
“And you shall tell them: These are the offerings you shall bring to the Lord: two year-old lambs without blemish each day, as a continual burnt offering.
You shall prepare one lamb in the morning, and you shall prepare the second lamb in the evening.
And you shall prepare a tenth of a measure of fine flour, mixed with a quarter of a measure of oil, for the regular burnt offering, as a sacrifice.
This is what shall take place on Mount Sinai, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And its drink offering shall be a quarter of a measure for each lamb. In the sanctuary you shall pour out a drink offering of strong drink to the Lord.
And you shall prepare the second lamb in the evening. You shall prepare it with its grain offering and its drink offering, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And on the Sabbath day you shall bring two year-old lambs without blemish, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its drink offering,
along with the burnt offering for the Sabbaths, on the Sabbaths, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
And on the first days of the months you shall bring a burnt offering to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each ram,
and one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb—a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma, as an offering to the Lord.

And their drink offering shall be half a measure for each bull, a third of a measure for each ram, and a quarter of a measure for each lamb. This is the burnt offering, month after month, throughout the months of the year.
And they shall prepare one male goat from the goats as a sin offering to the Lord, in addition to the continual burnt offering, with its drink offering.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord’s Passover.
And on the eighteenth day of the month is the feast. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
The first day shall be a holy assembly for you. You shall do no ordinary work.
You shall bring burnt offerings and food offerings to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs. They shall be without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
You shall prepare one tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs.
And one goat from the goats as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
This is in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is the continual burnt offering.
You shall prepare these on the seventh day as a gift and an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord. You shall also prepare the regular burnt offering with its drink offering.
The seventh day shall be designated as holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work on it.
On the day of the new harvest, when you bring the new grain offerings to the Lord at your Feast of Weeks, these days shall be designated as holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work on them.
You shall bring burnt offerings of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
The grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
And one tenth for each lamb.
And one male goat from the goats as a sin offering, a sacrifice for your deliverance.
You shall prepare these in addition to the regular burnt offering and their grain offering. These shall be holy for you, together with your drink offering.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, the day shall be designated as holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work on it. It shall be a day of signaling for you.
You shall prepare burnt offerings of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one young bull from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull and two tenths for each ram.
One tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs.
And one goat from the goats as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
These are in addition to the regular burnt offerings, according to their prescribed requirements, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And on the tenth day of this month, which is called holy for you, you shall humble yourselves. You shall not do any work of service.
You shall bring burnt offerings and offerings of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one young bull from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram.
One tenth for each lamb.

And one male goat from the goats as a sin offering to make atonement for you, in addition to the regular burnt offering that you shall give for the forgiveness of sins, together with its grain offering and its drink offering. He shall offer them according to the prescribed requirements as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, it shall be called holy for you. You shall not do any work of service on it. You shall celebrate a festival to the Lord for seven days.

You shall bring burnt offerings and an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord. On the first day you shall bring thirteen young bulls from the herd, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs. They shall be without blemish.
Their grain offerings shall be fine flour mixed with oil: one tenth for each of them and two tenths for each ram.
One tenth for each lamb, for the fourteen lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
And on the second day you shall bring with you twelve bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offering and drink offering for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
And on the third day you shall bring with you eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offering and drink offering with the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one goat from the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And on the fourth day you shall bring ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
And on the fifth day you shall bring nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
And on the sixth day you shall bring eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
And on the seventh day you shall bring seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
And on the eighth day you shall have a closing assembly. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And you shall bring burnt offerings and offerings presented as a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lamb, according to their number and the prescribed requirement.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings.

These you shall prepare for the Lord at your festivals, besides your vows and your burnt offerings, and those you will bring voluntarily, and your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.
And Moses spoke to the children of [?] according to everything that the Lord had commanded him.
And Moses spoke to the leaders of our children of [?], saying, “This is the word that the Lord has commanded.”
Any man who makes a vow to the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction on himself, or dishonors his word, must do everything that comes out of his mouth.
If a woman makes a vow to the Lord or imposes restrictions while she is a young girl in her father’s house,

and her father hears her vow and the restrictions she has imposed on herself, and her father remains silent toward her, all the vows she has made will stand as binding on her, and the restrictions she has imposed on herself will remain binding on her.

But if her father objects on the day he hears, all her vows and the restrictions she has imposed on herself will stand as binding on her, and the Lord will clear her of guilt, because her heart turned back.
But if she comes to live with her husband and makes vows binding on herself according to the words of her lips—the restrictions she has imposed on herself—
If her husband hears and remains silent toward her on the day when he hears, then all her vows and the obligations she has imposed on herself shall remain binding on her.

but if her husband objects on the day he hears, none of her vows or the restrictions she has imposed on herself will remain binding on her, because her husband has objected to her, and the Lord will clear her of guilt.
And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vows for herself—will remain binding on her.
But if her vow or her restriction was made in her husband’s house, binding herself,
With an oath, if her husband hears and remains silent toward her and does not oppose her, all her vows and all the obligations she has imposed on herself shall remain binding on her.

but if her husband explicitly cancels it on the day he hears, nothing that comes out of her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions she has imposed on herself will remain binding on her, because her husband has canceled them, and the Lord will clear her of guilt.
Every vow and every oath [?] to humble herself, her husband may establish as binding on her, and her husband may also cancel them.

But if he remains silent toward her from day to day, he will establish them as binding on her. He will establish her vows and the restrictions binding on her, because he remained silent toward her on the day he heard.
But if he explicitly takes them away from her after the day on which he made a vow and heard about it, he will bear his sin.
These are the regulations that the Lord commanded Moses concerning a man and his wife, and concerning a father and his daughter while she is a young girl in her father’s house.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Take vengeance for the Israelites against the people of Midian. Afterward you will be gathered to your people.”
Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Equip men from among you to go out to fight before the Lord against Midian. Take vengeance on Midian on behalf of the Lord.
Send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to go out to fight.”
And from the thousands of Israel, a thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand going out to fight.
Moses sent them out to fight, a thousand from each tribe, with their army, and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, with the sacred equipment and the signal trumpets in their hands.
They went out to fight against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.

They also killed the kings of Midian along with those they slew: Evi, Zur, Rekem, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with a sword, along with those they slew.
They took the women of Midian, their households, their livestock, everything they owned, and their wealth.
They plundered them, and they burned with fire all their towns where they lived and their encampments.
They took all their goods and all their plunder, both people and livestock.
They brought them—the captives, the plunder, and the equipment—to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the Israelites, into the camp on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses became angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who were returning from the fighting in the war.
Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the women alive?”

All these women were involved with the Israelites, following Balaam’s advice, to turn them away and make them neglect the word of the Lord concerning Peor. And the plague struck the congregation of the Lord.
Now then, you have killed the males among the whole multitude. But you must kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But keep alive all the women who have not slept with a man.

And you must stay outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who kills and everyone who touches someone who has been killed must purify themselves on the third day and on the seventh day—you and your captives.
And you must purify every goatskin garment and every wooden utensil.
And Eleazar the priest said before the soldiers who had come out from the battle to the war, “This is the requirement of the law that the Lord commanded Moses:
Except for gold, silver, copper, iron, [?], [?], and [?],
everything that passes through fire will be purified, but it must also be purified with the water of purification. And everything that does not pass through fire must pass through water.
And you must wash your clothes on the third day and purify yourselves. After this you are to go,” he says,
“Count the captured spoils, both people and livestock—you, Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the families of the congregation.
And divide the spoils into halves: one half for the warriors who will go out to battle, and one half for the whole congregation.
And set aside from them the Lord’s tribute, from the soldiers who go out to fight: one individual out of every five thousand, from people and livestock, and from the cattle, sheep, and goats.
You must take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the firstfruits for the Lord.
And from the half of what the children of [?] give, take one out of fifty, from the people, the cattle, the sheep, and all the livestock.
And give them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the tent of testimony.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest did these things just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the remainder of the spoils that the soldiers had taken amounted to 607,500 sheep.
And the cattle numbered 72,000.
And the sheep numbered 600.
And the people, consisting of women who had not slept with a man, numbered 32,000 in all.
And the half allotted to those who went out to war, from the total number of sheep, was 337,500.
And the tribute that belonged to the Lord from the sheep numbered 675. And the cattle numbered 34,000.
And the Lord’s tribute numbered 72.
And the sheep numbered 40,500, and the Lord’s tribute numbered 601.
And the people numbered 14,000, and the Lord’s tribute was 32 people.
And Moses gave the Lord’s tribute, the offering to God, to Eleazar the priest, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
From the half belonging to the Israelites, which Moses separated from what the fighting men held.
The congregation’s half consisted of 37,500 sheep and 34,000 cattle.
The number of people was 14,000.
Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals from the Israelites’ half and gave them to the Levites who guarded the tabernacle of testimony, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
All those appointed to positions of authority—the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—came forward to Moses.
They said to Moses, “Your servants have counted the fighting men under their command, and none of them has died.
Here is our gift, which we have brought to the Lord: the gold objects each man found—[?], bracelets, finger rings, and earrings—to make atonement for us before the Lord.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all the crafted objects.
All the gold set apart for the Lord from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds amounted to 34,750 shekels.
Each of the fighting men had taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and the fighting men and brought it into the tabernacle of testimony as a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord.
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad had very large numbers of livestock. They saw the region of Jazer and the region of Gilead, and the place was suitable for raising livestock.
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad came forward and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, saying:
“Ataroth, Beroth, Jazer, Ambran, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sibmah, Adau, and Bairan—
the land that the Lord gave to the Israelites is a land suitable for raising livestock, and your servants have a great deal of livestock.”
They also said, “If we have found favor in your sight, give this land to your servants as a possession, and do not make us cross the Jordan.”
Moses said to the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad, “Will your brothers go to war while you stay here?
Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land that the Lord has given them?
Did your fathers not do this when I sent them to Kadesh-barnea to explore the land?
They went up to the valley of the grape cluster and explored the land, and they discouraged the Israelites from entering the land that the Lord had given them.
The Lord became furious with them that day.

He swore, saying, ‘The people who came out of Egypt, twenty years old and older, who know evil and good, will not see the land that I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh, who set himself apart, and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the Lord.’
The Lord became furious with Israel and scattered them in the wilderness for forty years, until the entire generation that did evil before the Lord had perished.
Look! You have risen up in your fathers’ place, a gathering of sinful people, to add still more to the Lord’s furious anger against Israel.
For you will turn away from him, continuing to leave him behind in the wilderness, and you will act wickedly against this whole congregation.”
They came forward to him and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for the livestock and towns for our dependents.”
And we will arm ourselves and go ahead of the children of [?] until we bring them into their place. But our dependents will remain in fortified towns because of the people living in the land.
We will not return to our homes until the children of [?] have each received their share of the inheritance.
And we will not receive an inheritance among them on the other side of the Jordan or beyond it, because we have received our allotted inheritance on the eastern side of the Jordan.
Moses said to them, “If you act according to this word, if you arm yourselves before the Lord for war,”
Let every armed man among you cross the Jordan before the Lord until his enemy is destroyed before him.
Let them take possession of the land before the Lord, and afterward you may return. You will be free of guilt before the Lord and [?], and this land will be yours as a possession before the Lord.
But if you do not do these things, you will sin before the Lord, and you will recognize your sin when evil overtakes you.
Build yourselves towns for your dependents and folds for your livestock, and do what you have promised with your mouths.
The children of Reuben and the children of Gad said to Moses, “Your servants will do as our lord commands us.”
Our dependents, our wives, and all our livestock will remain in the towns of Gilead.
“But all your servants will cross over, armed and equipped before the Lord for war, as the Lord says.”
And Moses gave instructions concerning them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the families of the tribes of [?].

Moses said to them, “If the children of Reuben and the children of Gad cross the Jordan with you, every one of them armed for battle before the Lord, and you take possession of the land before you, you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.”

But if they do not cross with you armed for battle before the Lord, let their dependents, their wives, and their livestock cross ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and let them receive an inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.
The children of Reuben and the children of Gad answered, “We will do just what the Lord tells his servants.”
We will cross, armed, before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and you will give us our possession on this side of the Jordan.

And Moses gave the children of Gad, the children of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, belonging to the children of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its towns and its boundaries, the towns of the surrounding land.
And the children of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
and Shophan and Jazer. They raised them up,
and Abran and Beth-haran, fortified towns, and folds for the sheep.
And the children of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim.
And Baal-meon, which was enclosed, and Sibmah. They gave their own names to the cities they had built.
And the son of Machir, son of Manasseh, went to Gilead, captured it, and destroyed the Amorites who lived in it.
And Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
And Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their towns, and he called them the villages of Jair.
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and he called them Naboth after his own name.
And these are the camps of the children of [?] when they came out of the land of Egypt with their army, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
And Moses recorded their stages of travel and their camps at the Lord’s command. These are the camps along their journey.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the second day of Passover, the son of [?] went out with an uplifted hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.
The Egyptians were burying everyone among them who had died, whom the Lord had struck down: every firstborn in the land of Egypt. The Lord also executed judgment on their gods.
The children of [?] set out from Rameses and came to Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and came to Etham, which is part of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and came to the entrance of Pi-hahiroth, which is opposite Baal-zephon, and camped opposite Migdol.

They set out from opposite Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. They traveled for three days through the wilderness of the mountain and came to the bitter places.
They set out from the bitter places and came to Elim. There were twelve springs of water and seventy date palms in Elim, and they camped there beside the water.
They set out from Elim and came to the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and came to the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and came to Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and came to Elim.
They set out from Elim and came to Rephidim. There was no water there for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at the Graves of Craving.
They set out from the Graves of Craving and came to Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and came to Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and came to Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and came to Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and came to Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and came to Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and came to Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and came to Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and came to Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and came to Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and came to Terah.
They set out from Terah and came to Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and came to Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and came to Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and came to Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and came to Mount Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Mount Hor-haggidgad and came to Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and came to Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and came to Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and came to the wilderness of Zin. They set out from the wilderness of Zin and came to the wilderness of Paran, which is Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor, near the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up there at the Lord's command and died in the fortieth year after the children of [?] came out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, on the first day of the month.
Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the land of Canaan, heard that the children of [?] were coming into the land.
They set out from Mount Hor and came to Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and came to Punon.
They set out from Punon and came to Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and came to Gai, at the edge of the territory of Moab.
They set out from Gai and came to Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and came to Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and came to the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and came to the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
They camped beside the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, near the plains of Moab.
The Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, saying:
“Speak to the children of [?] and tell them: You will cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
You must destroy all its inhabitants before you and tear down their strongholds. You must destroy all their cast idols and remove all their pillars from there.
You must destroy all the inhabitants of the land and settle in it, for I have given you their land as an allotted possession.

You must inherit their land by lot according to your tribes. Give a larger possession to those who are numerous and a smaller possession to those who are few. The place for which a person's name is drawn will belong to him, for you will inherit according to your tribes and your ancestral families.

But you shall destroy the inhabitants of the land before you. Those whom you leave behind among them shall become splinters in your eyes and arrows in your sides, and they shall be your enemies in the land where you will live.
And just as I intended to do to them, so I will do to you.”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“Command the children of [?] and tell them: You will enter the land of Canaan. This will be your inheritance: the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
Your western side will extend from the wilderness of Zin as far as the region near Edom. Your western boundaries will begin at the portion of the Salt Sea on the eastern side.

And your boundaries will turn from the west along a road going up to Akrabbim, and will pass through Zin. Its course will be west of Kadesh-barnea, and it will go south of Arad and pass through Azmon.
And the boundary will turn from Azmon toward the Wadi of Egypt, and its course will reach the sea.
And your sea boundary will be the Great Sea. This will be your boundary along the sea.
And this will be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you yourselves will measure to the foot of the mountain.
And from the mountain to the mountain you will measure toward the entrance to Hamath, and its course will reach the boundaries of Zedad.
And it will enter the boundaries of Ziphron, and its course will reach Hazar-enan. This will be your northern boundary.
And you yourselves will measure your eastern boundaries from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
And the boundaries will descend from Shepham to Bela, from the east above the springs. And the boundaries of Bela will descend along the eastern side of the Sea of Chinnereth.
And the boundaries will descend to the Jordan, and their course will reach the Salt Sea. This land will be yours, with its surrounding boundaries.
And Moses commanded the Israelites, saying, “This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, as the Lord commanded, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
And the tribe of the descendants of Gad received their inheritance according to their ancestral households, and the half-tribe of Manasseh received their inheritance.
The tribes [?] received their inheritances on the bank of the Jordan opposite Jericho, on the southeastern side.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
“These are the names of the men who will inherit the land: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
[?] You are to choose one leader from each tribe so that you may inherit the land.
And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chelon;
from the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli;
from the descendants of Joseph, the leader of the tribe of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Susi;
the leader of the descendants of Ephraim, Samuel son of Sabath;
the leader of the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
the leader of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan;
the leader of the tribe of Asher, Achior son of Shelomi;
the leader of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Bemihud.
These are the men about whom the Lord spoke, that they should divide the land of Canaan among the descendants of [?].
And the Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Command the children of [?] to give the Levites cities to live in from the allotted lands they possess. They shall also give the Levites the land outside the cities that surrounds them.
The cities shall be theirs to live in, and their surrounding lands shall be for their four-footed livestock.
And the lands allotted to the cities that you will give to the Levites shall extend from the city wall outward for two thousand cubits all around.

You shall measure outside the city: two thousand cubits along the eastern side, two thousand cubits on the western side, two thousand cubits along the side toward the sea, and two thousand cubits along the northern side. Your cities shall be in the middle of these, together with the boundaries of the cities.

Among the cities you shall give the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall provide so that anyone who kills someone may flee there. In addition to these, you shall give another forty-two cities.
All the cities you shall give the Levites shall total forty-eight.

The cities you shall give shall come from the land possessed by the children of [?]. From those who received much, you shall give much, and from those who received little [?]. Each shall give the Levites some of their cities according to the inheritance they have inherited.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the children of [?] and tell them: You will cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
You shall set aside cities for yourselves to serve as places of refuge, so that anyone who kills someone, anyone who takes a life unintentionally, may flee there.
The cities shall serve you as places of refuge from the blood relative, so that the person who killed someone does not die before standing before the assembly for judgment.
The cities shall serve you as places of refuge.
You shall provide three cities beside the Jordan, and you shall provide the other three cities in the land of Canaan.

They shall be places of refuge for the children of [?], for the convert, and for the foreigner among you. These cities shall serve you as places of refuge, so that anyone who takes a life unintentionally may flee there.
But if someone strikes another person with an iron implement and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
But if someone throws a stone from his hand that can cause death, strikes another person with it, and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
But if someone strikes another person with a wooden implement in his hand that can cause death, and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
The blood relative shall kill the person who committed the killing. When he encounters him, he shall put him to death.
But if, out of hostility, he pushes him and throws any object at him with treachery, and he dies,
Or if someone strikes another person with his hand out of hatred, and that person dies, the one who struck him must be put to death. He is a murderer. The one who struck him must be put to death.
But if someone suddenly pushes another person, not out of hostility and not being angry with him, or throws any implement at him without deceit,
or, without realizing it, causes any stone capable of killing to fall on him, and he dies, although he did not wish it and was not seeking to harm him,
the assembly shall judge between the one who struck him and the blood relative according to these judgments.

the congregation shall rescue the one who killed him from the hand of the blood avenger. The congregation shall return him to the city to which he fled for refuge, and he shall remain there until the high priest dies, the one who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the person who killed someone goes outside the boundaries of the city to which he fled,
and the blood relative finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge, and the blood relative of the person who was killed kills him, he will be guilty.
He shall live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the high priest dies, the person who killed someone shall return to the land he possesses.
These shall be legal statutes for you throughout your generations, in all the places where you live.
Anyone who kills a person—you shall put the killer to death on the testimony of witnesses. But a single witness must not testify against a person to have that person put to death.
And you must not [?] in exchange for the life of the killer if he is condemned to death, for he must certainly die.
You must not accept a ransom from him so that he may flee to that city and live on the land until the high priest dies.
You must not fill the land where you live with murder. The land [?] from the blood spilled on it, except through the blood of the one who spills it.

The leaders of the tribe of the descendants of Gad, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of the descendants of Joseph, came forward. They spoke before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders of the families of the children of [?].

The daughters of Zelophehad did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
